denominator: Two counts over [window], both restricted to Gravity Forms form_id=1 (the /contact/ form): (A) origin OpenLiteSpeed access-log lines matching an HTTP POST to path /contact/, counted by concatenating every retained access.log* file on i-0152e3fe2599fa630 whose lines fall inside [window] and grepping the literal string 'POST /contact/' (verbatim path match; no query-string variant was observed); (B) Gravity Forms entry-store rows in wp_gf_entry for form_id=1 whose date_created falls inside [window], read via `wp db query` over SSM (root, WP-CLI 2.12.0). Each count is split into AUTOMATED vs HUMAN-LIKE by the discriminator below; a per-day rate (count / window-days) is carried alongside the raw count so that a before-window and an after-window of unequal length stay comparable.
discriminator: A submission (an access-log line, by its User-Agent request-header field; or a GF entry, by its stored user_agent column) is classed AUTOMATED if that User-Agent string (i) is wrapped in a literal escaped double-quote pair -- the WHOLE declared browser string begins AND ends with a raw " character, an artifact no real browser ever emits on its own UA header and which a form-spam tool's templated UA literal produced here -- or (ii) contains a case-insensitive 'bot' token or a self-declared non-browser client string (e.g. 'DomainIntelBot/1.0'). Otherwise HUMAN-LIKE. MEASURED, not assumed: every quoted-UA/bot-token hit in the access log matches a quoted-UA/bot-token row in the GF entry store at the same source IP and the same timestamp (8 of 8 cross-checked in this baseline read), and several flagged addresses (185.220.100.253, 185.220.100.255, 185.220.101.174 among them) fall in the 185.220.100.0/22 range historically documented as Tor exit-node infrastructure -- offered as CORROBORATING, not load-bearing, since no live IP-reputation vendor lookup was run (none is authorized for this task). THE STATUS-CODE TRAP NAMED IN THE TASK ORDER'S GROUNDING SECTION DOES NOT APPLY TO THIS ENDPOINT: WordPress's failed-login-returns-200/success-returns-302 asymmetry is a wp-login.php behavior specific to that form; Gravity Forms submits form 1 via gform_submission_method=iframe, so BOTH an accepted and a rejected /contact/ POST return HTTP 200 from the origin alike (confirmed: all 53 in-window log lines read status 200, including the ones that never produced a stored entry) -- status code carries NO discriminating signal for this endpoint and none is used here.
